ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: wardens, the Bell, the Circuit and the Wheel
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Four more peoples, none of them anyone's enemy by nature: the Lantern Wardens who hunt the region's great beasts, the Quiet Bell who keep the dead of every people, the Circuit of Tamers who walk the region with their companions, and the Wheel, a salvage town that never stops moving. Each has its own founding, gear, faith, towns and words, and comes to the colony's gate in its own ways.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: They are among the world's peoples when a new world is made, once each, at the game's usual chances; remove them in the world's faction list like any other people. A save made before them meets them when one of them arises during play.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: All four defend their towns and raid only when the colony has turned them hostile, by the game's own rules, and seldom then. Their notables have titles of their own, their messengers words of their own, and their towns a plan of their own when the land suits it. They arise in every age: a people of their ways that arose among an industrial town's survivors carries that age's weapons.

li.heading: Who they are

table.li: People | Lives by | Age | On the map | Their towns

The Lantern Wardens | Hunting the great beasts | Medieval | Furs and oiled leather of every make under a hood dyed lantern red; trackers with bows and crossbows, spear-wardens with boar-spears | Palisaded lodges with a trophy hall, kennels and a lantern post on every road out

The Quiet Bell | Keeping the dead of every people | Medieval | Bell-keepers in one grey habit and veil; sextons and gravewardens plainly and differently, in grey hoods or the gravewardens' grey cape and helmet | Walled grave-gardens with an ossuary, a bell tower and a quiet hostel

The Circuit of Tamers | Taming beasts and friendly bouts | Industrial | Travelling clothes of every make with a violet sash of tokens; ring-wardens in one kit of jacket and helmet | Bout-rings, a hatchery and stables for every kind

The Wheel | Salvage, mending and the road | Industrial | Patched coats of every cut in old brass with the cog on the shoulder, tool belts; yard guards in one kit of brass jacket and flak | A yard inside a ring of carts, laid out as if leaving tomorrow; it moves on every month or so

li.after: With Ideology each keeps a faith of its own (the lit crossroads, the quiet ground, the freely given bond, the turning wheel) and its own style; with Biotech each has a share of other kinds of people. With Vanilla Ideology Expanded's memes their faiths take its light, its exalted priesthood, its nomads and its scrappers too.

li.heading: Where their ways began
li.text: Each keeps a founding story, a few sayings, and what it honours and fears, shown on their card and spoken in their letters, messengers, visitors and talk.

points.li: The Lantern Wardens began with Tobin Garrow, a shepherd whose village was emptied in one night by something out of the treeline. He hung his dead brother's lantern at the crossroads and kept it lit until the beast was dead, which took eleven years. A Warden still ties a knot in a red cord for every beast felled, and keeps a book with a page for each.

The Quiet Bell began after the long war, when nobody would bury the raiders in the fields and what came up out of them taught the region why that matters. A widow named Ysolde Marr buried them one by one with a cracked chapel bell, ringing once over every grave, friend or foe.

The Circuit of Tamers began with Nessa Pell, a herder girl who found an egg in a falling star's crater, raised what hatched, and walked the region with it for forty years, challenging every keeper of beasts she met. Their highest honour is to be beaten fairly by a stranger.
The Wheel began the night its valley burned, when the wheelwright Mab Wainwright put her house on her cart and drove out ahead of the fire with the others behind her. Nobody has ever voted to stop.

li.heading: What they wear, carry and know
li.text: No two of them look alike: each people wears its colour on a piece or two, its soldiers one kit where it has soldiers, and its civilians whatever their age and calling would, from the game, the DLCs and the mods loaded. A few have a gift (A RimWorld of Magic's classes, a psylink).

points.li: The Lantern Wardens: no uniform at all but the red hood; trackers with bows, great bows and crossbows (Vanilla Weapons Expanded, Medieval 2's arbalest) and quivers, spear-wardens with spears and pikes. A few are rangers or snipers of A RimWorld of Magic; the lantern-master may be a Wildspeaker of Vanilla Psycasts Expanded. In the industrial and spacer ages their trackers hunt with guns. They carry pemmican, herbs or a spare hide.

The Quiet Bell: the bell-keepers' grey habit (a robe, or Medieval 2's mantle) and veil, a few of them priests of A RimWorld of Magic; sextons with spades (Vanilla Weapons Expanded's shovel) and clubs, now and then a geomancer; gravewardens in grey cape and helmet with maces and hammers, a few paladins, and in the industrial and spacer ages firebombs or an incinerator (Anomaly) for what will not stay down. They carry linen for shrouds.

The Circuit of Tamers: the violet sash (Biotech's sash and bandolier) over travelling clothes; every tamer good with beasts, a few druids or summoners of A RimWorld of Magic, and in the spacer age a few Wildspeakers. Their rangers carry rifles, or bows in the tribal and medieval ages; hounds and wolves fight beside them. They carry kibble and hay.

The Wheel: coats of any cut in old brass, tool belts and packs (Vanilla Apparel Expanded - Accessories), scrap-built guns (Vanilla Weapons Expanded - Makeshift) and wrenches; a mechanitor or two with Biotech's mechlink and headset; technomancers of A RimWorld of Magic now and then. In the tribal and medieval ages their guards carry hammers and maces, in the spacer age salvaged lasers. They carry components, steel and chemfuel.

With A RimWorld of Magic a caster among them looks like one, and the Quiet Bell, built on what should not stir, has more of them than most peoples: its bell-keepers' priests in a disciple hood, its gravewardens' paladins in the Helm of the Valiant, its sextons' geomancers in a hood of protection; the tamers' druids and summoners in a hood of protection; the Wardens' rangers and the Wheel's technomancers have no garb of their own in the mod. The Bell's priests and paladins may heal one of the colony's hurt, the tamers' druids cure an infection or a flu. A visitor with a class names their craft to the first of the colony they meet, who remarks on it; a colonist who sees a raider's caster names it too. Their card says what crafts are among them, and their letters mention them now and then. Now and then a visitor who is content, or of a people allied with the colony, casts a helpful spell for it with the mod's own effects, once a visit at most; in a fight they cast by the mod's own AI and settings, its most broken spells kept out.

Their kinds of people (Biotech) are a real mix and still mostly baseliners: Venators, yttakin, saurids and wood elves with the Wardens; dirtmoles, fungoids, stoneborn and dark elves with the Bell; animusen, saurids and animakin with the Circuit; wasters, dirtmoles, androids, boglegs and starjacks with the Wheel.

The Lantern Wardens: when a pack's alpha, a beast nemesis or a legend of the region is on the colony's land, two or three Wardens may come to hunt it, alone or beside the colony's best shot; when it falls, one of them skins it where it lies, the hide going into their book and the meat left for the colony. Their pelt-buyer buys the colony's pelts at a little over their worth, and a tracker may teach someone to read a trail. When a beast has taken one of the colony, a Warden comes to light a lantern at the gate for them through the night, and those who loved them may stand it with the Warden. Their lodge may ask for two good shots for a drive.

The Quiet Bell: after a fight, with the enemy's dead still lying out, bell-keepers come to bury them beyond the wall or carry them off, the Bell's words said over each, and the raiders' own people think a little better of the colony for it. A bell-keeper may lead the funeral of one of the colony at their grave. With Anomaly, when the void is awake, an old bell-keeper may warn that the ground is listening and stand at the gate with a lamp, or the colony may keep a watch on its walls. In a plague year their grave-gardens ask for linen for shrouds. The undertakers come from them likeliest.

The Circuit of Tamers: a roaming tamer may challenge the colony's best hand with beasts to a friendly bout with their companion (a Fighting type with PokéWorld, else a beast of the land): practice blows each way by the Fighting-type spar's rules, the winner by skill with beasts and hands, and one bout in 25 a bruise. Beaten fairly, the tamer hands over an egg of their hatchery. An egg-trader swaps or sells eggs of a kind the colony doesn't keep. A ranger may bring home one of the colony's animals that strayed. They may ask the colony to raise a young beast of their stables for a season. The animal doctor comes from them likeliest.

The Wheel: their fixer mends the colony's worn clothes and weapons for silver, one piece at a time; scrap-runners buy slag and broken things, carried out to their cart, for silver or a piece they mended back to new; a mechanoid's wreck near the colony brings them at a run to strip it for parts, half for the colony, or bought whole. Their yard may ask for steel or parts for a broken axle. The travelling tinker comes from them likeliest.

li.heading: Their towns, and new peoples like them

points.li: The Wardens' lodge, the Bell's grave-garden, the Circuit's ring and the Wheel's yard are laid out to their plans when a town's map is made; where the land is too wet or rough for it, the game makes its own base.
The Wheel's towns move on: every month or so each rolls a few tiles to new ground, never while the colony has a map of it, a caravan bound for it or an open quest about it, and the news says where.

New peoples that arise during play may take their ways: survivors of a fallen town who stay to bury its dead (a quarter of them) keep the Bell's ways, and in the industrial and spacer ages a third of the rest put what is left on wheels as the Wheel does; a band of the banished led by one good with beasts walks the region as tamers, by a good shot as wardens.

li.heading: Of their own: gifts, trust and camps

points.li: The Lantern Wardens' lantern post: while a legend, a beast nemesis or a pack's alpha is on the colony's land, three Wardens and two hounds (a German shepherd with Vanilla Animals Expanded) may camp at the edge nearest it for up to ten days. They light the lantern every night and watch the beast from its trail by day, warn the colony when it comes close to the walls, and ask for meat for the hounds. Asked, they take the colony's best shot out on the trail: two of them after it under the game's own assault, the colonist on the game's own hunt; if it falls, one of them skins it where it lies. It can turn: one night the beast comes to their fire (the game's fight, the colony told so it can run to help), or a hound runs off on the trail. When the beast falls, or the trail goes cold, the lantern goes out and the page is written.

The Wardens and the Circuit together: with a legend or an alpha on the land (never a beast that took a person), the Wardens and a tamer of the Circuit can reach the gate the same day. Side with the hunt and the Wardens hunt it with the colony's best shot; side with the taming and it is marked for the game's own taming, the colony's best hand with beasts trying with the tamer beside them, its revenge on a failed try at the game's own chance; or let them settle it in a bout at the gate, the winner by their hands: the Wardens hunt it alone, or the tamer tries to win it over for the Circuit and lead it home. The side passed over thinks less of the colony, a bout's loser a little, and the region hears of it.

The Lantern Wardens' page in the book: some hours after one of the colony brings down a legend of the region, a beast nemesis or a pack's alpha, a keeper of the book comes to write it in and tie a red cord on the hunter's sleeve at the gate (a red cord shows on their health). The hunter keeps a lasting good memory and the Wardens' word on them, and gets the Hunter expertise with Vanilla Skills Expanded, else a passion in the skill that made the kill; the Wardens give +6, and buy the pelt for their hall at twice its worth.

Wardens at the manhunt: when a manhunting pack or a mad beast of a size besets the colony, two to four Wardens may come running in from the edge nearest the beasts and fight beside the colony, the game's own fight. When the beasts are down they skin what they brought down and keep the hides, the meat left for the colony, or keep everything if the colony offers; or the colony thanks them and they go. Their arms are their age's. +3.

The hive burned: when insects dig in near the colony (the game's hives, or Vanilla Factions Expanded - Insectoids 2's wild hives and burrows), three to five Wardens come with fire: torches, molotovs, or an incendiary launcher by their age. Together, they wait at the edge for the colony's drafted fighters to come up, then go in; alone, they go in at once; or they keep watch at the edge for a day in case. The insects defend the hive, and fire can spread.

The Circuit of Tamers' beast-doctor: for a beast of the colony's that lost a leg, the Circuit fits Alpha Implants' animal prosthetic leg where it stands in an industrial or spacer age, by the game's own surgery and its chance; in any age the beast-doctor can take the beast to the Circuit's stables to live out its days, leading it away, and leave the young one of its kind brought along.

The field that stirs (with Anomaly): when bodies left lying on the colony's land get up again as shamblers, three gravewardens of the Quiet Bell may come running from the edge nearest them and fight them, the game's own fight; their arms are their age's (maces and spades, firebombs and flamers from the industrial age). When the shamblers are down they dig a grave for each beyond the wall and ring the bell over every grave. The colony may promise to bury its dead from now on (the Bell is warmer, and hears of it if its dead rise again within the year), or thank them and they go.

Mourners from the other side: a season after the Bell buried raiders the colony killed in graves beyond its wall, a bell-keeper brings two mourners of the raiders' people to the gate (as the Bell's guests if their people are at war with the colony). Let through, they stand an hour at the graves while the bell is rung, and their people think a little better of the colony, more if one of the colony stands with them; a people at war may then offer a truce by its own letter. Turned away, the Bell is saddened.

A grave-garden for the colony: two sextons of the Bell lay flagstones of the land's own stone between three or more of the colony's graves, plant roses beside them and set up a bell-post over three days, for six meals (or only the bell-post, in an afternoon). While the post stands, anyone resting in its ground finds it quiet (a good mood), a funeral at one of its graves is remembered as a fuller rite and the post is rung at its end, and with Anomaly a body lying in its ground does not rise (with the deeper game hooks on).

The field of the fallen: after a fight leaves a dozen dead or more on the colony's land, bell-keepers and sextons of the Bell camp three to six days, dig a row of graves beyond the wall, lay the dead in them and ring the bell at each dusk. They ask for wood and cloth. Mourners of the dead's peoples come to stand at the graves, and each of those peoples thinks better of the colony. It can turn: with Anomaly and the void awake the dead still lying out may rise, or the dead's people come for them, asking at the gate if they are at peace with the colony (let them take their dead home, talk them into leaving them with the Bell, or refuse), or as a band against the camp if they are at war with it and the Bell.

The Circuit's bond freely given: a roaming tamer spends an afternoon with one of the colony's animals that still has tasks to learn, the colony's best hand with animals kept at its side. It learns every task it can and bonds with that hand, its master; the hand gets a lesson, and the Trainer expertise with Vanilla Skills Expanded. With PokéWorld a Pokémon of the colony's is chosen first. Once a colonist.

An egg from the crater: a tamer brings a rare egg of a beast that does not live near the colony, from Dinosauria, Megafauna, ReGrowth, Alpha Animals or PokéWorld first, else the game's own, and asks the colony to hatch it. It has to be kept warm until it hatches (a cold egg spoils, as any does). Whoever of the colony spends the most time near it, or carries it, is the one it bonds with when it hatches; a season later the tamer comes back to see it grown and works with it for an hour.

The Circuit's ring: while a great fair runs in the region, six to ten tamers pitch a bout-ring by torchlight by the colony for four to six days, with their animals (Pokémon with PokéWorld). Each afternoon the colony may send up to two of its people to challenge one of their animals in a friendly bout, by the bout's own rules: the winner by handling and melee, a lesson in handling, and one bout in twenty-five a bruise, shown. When they leave, the colony's challenger with the most wins has the Circuit's token tied on, an egg of their hatchery, and the region hears of it.

The Wheel's night crew: the night after a raid, a fixer and a crew with lamps may come to mend the colony's damaged walls, doors, turrets and furniture by morning, each back to whole, while one of them gathers the raiders' broken gear lying about. Paid in that gear and a little silver, or in silver alone and the colony keeps the gear. They are gone by first light.

Made better: a fixer of the Wheel takes one colonist's own weapon or armour (below masterwork) out to their cart beyond the edge of the land for a day, paid in silver and steel or in silver alone. They bring it back a quality better (masterwork at most) and fully mended, worn or carried again as before; should the fixer not come back, a runner brings it to the gate. Once a colonist.

A wagon of the colony's own (with Vehicle Framework and Vanilla Vehicles Expanded): a fixer builds the colony a vehicle of its age at the gate over a day, from its own goods carried out to them (wood and some steel for the wagon before the industrial age, steel and components for a small truck after) and silver for the work; the colony's crafter may work beside them and learn.

The Wheel stops by: when a Wheel town's move brings it within a few tiles of the colony, its yard may camp three days at the edge of the land, with its pack animals, a mending tent and a scrap market (trade with them as with any trader). The colony can sell its scrap and have its worn things mended for silver. It can turn: a fixer and one of the colony argue over a price at the stall (the yard less friendly, its mending a little dearer), or the yard decides to stay two days longer.

Breaking the drought: in a drought (Odyssey's or Vanilla Events Expanded's) or a heat wave, two storm-walkers of the Stormglass Conclave may come to the gate. For silver they set two rods on the colony's high ground at dusk and keep the night beside them, the colony's best at the fields with them if the colony likes (a lesson, and a season of reading the glass); at first light the dry spell ends and the land's own rain begins, one time in four as a thunderstorm with its own lightning. Then they take their rods down and go.

The tide read: while the Conclave watches the colony's sky (their season's watch), a psychic drone or soothe is held back a day like a condition of the sky, and the vial-runner's warning names everyone it will touch. When a drone the watch foresaw comes, a reader comes to sit an hour with the one it touches worst, or with the two worst one after the other: a calm hour remembered while the drone lasts.

The storm tower: in spring and summer, two readers and an apprentice of the Conclave may camp a week on the colony's high ground with a glass mast and two rods, writing down every storm; lightning that falls near the rods strikes them without fire. The colony's best at the fields may sit their night watch (a lesson, and a season of reading the glass). They leave a sealed vial and the season's forecast (the Conclave's watch, free for a season). It can turn: a bolt in a storm may land past their rods and start a fire, which they beat out, or their apprentice may take a chill, shown.

Fire in the canopy: when a wildfire burns among the colony's trees, three to five thorn-guards of the Mossborn may come running from the edge nearest it and beat it out beside the colony's people, fire by fire (the game's own beating, its burns the fire's own). The colony may ask them back to replant the burn once it is out, or thank them and they go. +4.

Seeds of the old wood: an herb-trader of the Mossborn brings seeds of a plant the colony doesn't grow, the player's plant mods first (Vanilla Plants Expanded and its add-ons, Alpha Biomes), the game's own after. For silver, or a share of the colony's harvest, they sow a plot of it near the fields with the colony's best grower beside them, who learns how it is grown; the plot is the colony's growing zone of that plant from then on.

After the fire: after a wildfire leaves ten burned trees or more on the colony's land, or a blight takes six of its plants, a grove-warden and seed-carriers of the Mossborn may camp a week in the burn. They cut the burned trees (the wood is the colony's) or the blighted plants, plant saplings across the burn (the colony's planting in their ledger), and sing at their fire at night. They ask for food, and that the colony fell no tree within the planting while they are there: felling there is a wrong, and they leave. The colony's planter may plant beside them. It can turn: in dry, warm weather the fire may start again in the ash, and they beat it out.

A contract on the colony's enemy: a captain of the Ashen Banner offers to march against an enemy camp within reach (a hostile camp from the game's quests and sites, else a hostile town), at a price by the threat it is. The colony sends at least one of its fighters there by caravan within the contract's days, and the company comes in beside them when they get there and goes for the enemy. When it is over, half the silver found there goes to the company by the contract (unless their share was paid up front), and every name they lost is read on the Roll. Not reached in time, the company marches home with its pay.

An old soldier settles: a veteran of the Banner, past the age for the march, may ask to settle with the colony with a war-horse (the game's horse, Vanilla Genetics Expanded's Paragon horse in the spacer age) and the kit of the Banner's age; the horse is bonded and trained to them. Once a year the Banner calls them to its muster for a week (a caravan of one), or the colony pays a muster fee; refusing both costs goodwill. The musters may be bought out for good when they settle.

The other side's contract: when a people at war with the colony and at peace with the Banner sends a raid, the Banner may have been hired to march with it. The raid is held back a day while a sergeant comes under a white flag to say so. The colony may buy the contract (the company comes in on the colony's side when the raid does), pay them to stand aside (the raid comes without them), or let them march (the raid comes at the storyteller's own size, part of it the Banner's soldiers). If the raid never comes, the colony's silver is sent back.

A company on the march: eight to twelve soldiers of the Banner on their way to a contract may camp a night or two at the edge of the colony's land, bedrolls round their fire, and drill at dawn. They buy food (twenty meals at the gate if the colony likes). The sergeant drills the colony's fighters if asked, and asks whether one of them would enlist for the season (a caravan of one to the Banner's town, home with pay). A soldier may ask to stay, which the Banner holds against the colony. It can turn: the people they march against catches them here (a band against the camp; the colony may stand with them), or a bet at their fire ends in a brawl with one of the colony, shown.

The master's mark: when one of the colony makes a masterwork or a legend, a master of the Kiln Guild may come to the gate a day or more later to judge it where it is, the piece lying in the stores or held or worn by its maker. Let in, the master looks it over for an hour with its maker beside them (who learns from it with the second answer). True work gets the guild's mark: a good memory for the maker, the guild speaks well of them (the colony's renown reads it), and with Vanilla Skills Expanded the quality expertise for a piece made at a bench. One masterwork in five, one legend in twelve, has a fault the master finds and says so, which stings the maker.

Come back better: a year after a wander-year at the colony ended well, the same journeyman comes back to the gate a master of the guild, with a masterwork of their own making as a gift. The maker who taught them gets a lasting memory, and may sit with them a while or work a morning at the bench beside them and learn.

A work that stays: three journeymen of the guild may camp by the colony for five to eight days and build a great work with its own stone or wood: a carved bridge over the water nearest the colony (Kell's bridge, of the colony's stone with Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Architect, else the game's wooden one), else a grand statue, monument or sculpture in its largest dining or recreation room (Vanilla Furniture Expanded - Art, or the game's own), else a fountain where the colony gathers (Alpha Props - Parks, Dubs Bad Hygiene). Once they have camped the stone is carried out to them; they carve at it by day, and when it stands it is the colony's, excellent, with a journeyman's name on it. The colony's best at the art may work beside them. It can turn: a cracked block needs more stone (without it they wait a day or two, then make do and it stands a grade plainer), or a day's bad work is torn down.

A voice for the colony: once a season an operator of the Signal Line offers one call on the Line's masts at the Line's price: a trader of goods or of arms (the game's own caravan of that kind, from a people at peace that sends one), hands (someone comes to join), or a good word to the people the colony stands worst with. With a radio (a powered comms console, or the colony's own relay mast) the operator calls on it and it is answered within hours; without, a runner of the Line carries the call and it is answered in a day or two.

A mast at a friend's town: for a fee, in silver or components, a lineman raises one of the Line's masts at the town of a notable the colony writes to. A message says when it stands; from then the colony's letters to that town and the answers take half the days on the road, while the Line is at peace. The mast is lost with the town.

The line crew: three or four linesmen may camp a week on the colony's high ground and raise a working mast there (a flag-and-lamp tower if the Line is of the tribal or medieval age), stringing wire by day. While it stands the colony's letters go out by their wire in half the days, and once a night they pass on the region's news, the places it names marked as heard of. They ask for food and components, and the colony may keep their mast as its own relay mast for a fee. It can turn in a thunderstorm: a lineman may fall from the mast, or the lightning may break it, and they raise it again.

The pit's cave-in: when a pit of the Deepwell Union within reach caves in, a runner asks for the colony's best miner and its doctor. Sent, each sets out on the roads as a caravan of one and digs there for four to six days, a shift a day, learning. One shift in twenty a fall of rock may crush a foot or a hand (the union drill's own chance), told as word from the pit and bound there. Home again they bring the union's pay, a good memory, and the union thinks better of the colony.

Oil in the ground: with Rimefeller, and its wells open to the colony, a union assayer may have found the colony's oil (where Rimefeller's own well may be placed) and sink a well there for the colony, for silver or for a year's share (chemfuel collected each season for four seasons, its worth in silver when the stores are short). Without Rimefeller the assayer marks the deep seam nearest the colony for a small fee instead, and the union's drill crew comes for it the day after; the colony's best miner may walk the ground with them.

The organizer's evening: when the colony's people are worn down (the heart's strain, or long hours by decree), a shift-captain of the union may come at dusk and ask to speak at the colony's fire. The next morning the one most worn down brings a petition to the council: to lift the long hours, else for days of rest. Granted, those worn down are glad of it and the union thinks better of the colony; refused or left to lapse, they are stung.

The picket: when the union votes to strike, strikers may keep a picket camp by the colony's road for as long as the strike lasts, singing at their fire in the evening. Their shift-captain asks for food for the picket line, which settles the strike, and invites the colony's best miner to their fire. It can turn: strikebreakers of a people at war with the union may come against the camp (a band against a camp, the colony asked what to do). When the strike ends they march home singing.

An observer at the vote: on the morning of the colony's polling day a clerk of the Last Republic may ask to observe. Let in, the clerk walks the colony with the roll, a word with each voter, and stands by the count in the evening; while the clerk is there a heckle at the count comes to blows half as often. When the result is in the clerk calls the vote fair, and with a radio at home the colony hears the Republic's evening broadcast say so. The result may also go into the Republic's register, which pleases the council's members.

A medal: half a day to four days after one of the colony carries someone out of a fight or holds the line in a hard one, a clerk and a guard of the Republic may come to read a citation at the gate and pin the Republic's medal on them: a lasting good memory, the Republic remembering them by name (the colony's renown reads it), and from the industrial age on with Vanilla Books Expanded the Republic's newspaper with the citation in it. Whoever is free may come to hear it.

A fugitive of the Republic: a deserter of the Civic Guard may run to the gate asking to join, a detail of the Guard close behind. Pay the fine and take them in; shelter them (the Republic is angry and strikes the colony's papers, and if that turns it against the colony the detail fights); or hand them over and the detail leads them away, the Republic thanking the colony.

A ration post: in a famine in the region a clerk and two guards of the Republic may keep a ration post by the colony's road for a week. The hungry of the region come in from the road for a ration and walk on, now and then one asking the colony to take them in. The post buys food from the colony at the Republic's price, and a colony holding the Republic's papers may draw rations on its ration cards. It can turn: the rations run out with people waiting and the queue comes to blows, or the guards turn away someone of a people at war with the Republic.

The colony's gravship (with Odyssey): the Hollow Fleet may call the colony's gravship on its own channel. Its officers come down near it (by shuttle with Royalty, else by drop pod), walk its decks with the colony's pilot and enter it in the Fleet's log, leaving a part from the hull's stores (a ship's upgrade of Odyssey or Vanilla Gravship Expanded, else gravlite panels) or teaching the pilot the ship. The pilot is glad of it, and the Fleet thinks much better of the colony.

A sleeper of theirs: when the colony has found one of the old cryptosleep caskets on its land, a deck-runner of the Fleet may come for the sleeper in it, one of the ship's own. Handed over, the runner opens the casket and they walk home together, and the Fleet pays; kept, the colony opens it and the sleeper joins; left shut, the sleeper sleeps on, and finds their own way home if woken later.

The order to disembark (with Royalty): when one of the colony holds an Empire title of knight or higher, an officer of the Fleet may ask them to come to the hull and give the order the captain never gave. They go as a caravan of one; three to five of the crew may come home with them and join, and the rest settle near the hull as a people of their own, warm toward the colony.

A landing party: four to six of the Fleet's crew may camp by the colony for five to seven days, bunks in a row under one roof, the watch bell rung at the change of the watch, surveying the land by day for when the order comes. They buy food and offer their medic to the colony's sick, and once their watch may spot raiders coming and warn the colony a couple of hours ahead. It can turn: a sleeper they brought falls ill, or a deckhand asks to join the colony against the officer's wish.

A gene taken out (with Biotech): a sequencer of the Helix Works may offer to take a harmful gene out of one of the colony where they stand, two hours' work, for silver or a genepack. They need a little more food afterwards, and carry the game's mark of a xenogerm replicating for a while.

A whole xenogerm (with Biotech): a sequencer may offer one of the colony's baseliners a whole xenogerm of one of the Works' own kinds, for silver and two genepacks or all in silver. They lie in the game's xenogermination coma for some days afterwards; a faith that holds to its own kinds is named on the card.
A hybrid beast (with Vanilla Genetics Expanded): a vat-keeper may bring a young hybrid from the Works' vats to sell, the colony's handler its master, and show the handler how it is kept.

A field lab: two sequencers and a vat-keeper may camp by the colony for a week, sampling the land's beasts and plants. All week the colony may ask for their gene work or let them draw a sample, and sell them genepacks. It can turn: a beast of theirs gets loose and turns on whoever is near, or one of them falls ill and the colony's doctor may see to them.

Linked into the Lattice (with Biotech): a mech-tender of the Lattice may offer to link the colony's mechanitor into its own, two hours with the array where they stand. From then on the mechanitor commands two more bandwidth for as long as the Lattice stays at peace with the colony (the link goes quiet the day it doesn't), and now and then dreams another linked mind's dream, a small mood good or bad. Or a link for work only: one more bandwidth, no dreams.

A mech gone feral (with Biotech): one of the Lattice's light war mechs may slip its link and roam the colony's land, attacking whatever comes near, with two link-wardens at the gate after it. They can call it in over the link and relink it at the gate, and the Lattice pays for the trouble; or the colony takes it down with them (the game's own fight) and keeps the wreck for its parts; or they go home and it wanders off in a day or so.

A mech yard (with Biotech): a mech-tender, two link-hands and four to six labour mechs may camp by the colony for five to seven days. By day some of the mechs cut plain rock near the camp and the rest stack it, and the cut rock is left to the colony. The colony may hire the mechs for a day, the haulers carrying its loose things into its stockpiles and the rest mending its worn buildings. It can turn: a mech goes feral, or a band of a people at war with the Lattice comes for the mechs.

The hum deepened (with Royalty): at evening a cantor of the Choir may offer to sit through the night at the bed of a colonist with a psylink, humming while they lie listening, and by morning the psylink is a level higher (with Vanilla Psycasts Expanded, a point for one more power). A colonist without one but psychically sensitive wakes a first level instead. The price is a piece of the colony's art, or an evening in which the cantor listens to the colony: once the night is over most at home feel a calm, some an unease.

The void listens back (with Anomaly): a warden of the quiet may come for a colonist shaken by the void (with Vanilla Anomaly Expanded - Insanity, their sanity low; else a memory of the void on them) and stay at their side through the day; some of their sanity returns and the void's memories are lifted. At the end the warden says what kind of threat the void will send next, and the next such threat within the month is that one. Or the warden only listens an hour at the edge of the colony's land and gives the warning.

A mind that shouts: when one of the colony has been hours in a mental break that turns on nobody, a listener of the Choir may come to the gate, having heard it from the road, and sit beside them two hours (following if they wander) until it ends, calmly. Someone of the colony may sit with them and learn how.

A listening ring: three to five of the Choir may camp three to five days at the quietest place on the colony's land and sing each evening; late in the evening the colony feels it, a calm for most and an unease for some. A psycaster of the colony may sit with them and come back with a full focus. They ask that loud work be kept away from them at night. It can turn: with the void stirring their song goes strange one night, and they leave.

The seal broken: insects or mechs may get into the Sunken Vault's lower level, and a surface-runner brings the overseer's call for the colony's fighters. Two or more of the colony's grown people go to the vault's town by caravan within five days and fight beside the vault's security on the ground beside it (the game's own fight); won, the vault sets down a share of its last stores and remembers its town defended. Or the colony sends components and medicine instead.

The last part: when one of the colony has lost an eye or a limb and the colony has no part for it, the vault's medic may bring one of the vault's last bionics, for a large supply of components and food that holds the vault's age for a year. The medic fits it at the colony's bed by the game's own surgery, or hands it over for the colony's own doctor.

The console that talks to nobody: the vault's old console may pick up the colony's radio, and the overseer asks to talk with the colony's best talker at dusk for three evenings (without a radio, a runner brings a letter each evening and the talker writes back). At the end the overseer asks the colony for components or medicine, a runner coming for them, or tells where an old supply cache of the vault's lies a few tiles off.

Surface scouts: three of the vault's scouts may camp a week by the colony to learn the surface, asking each afternoon to be taught plants, animals or shooting; what they learn the vault keeps. They sell their last odds and ends, and one may ask to stay. It can turn: one is sky-sick and keeps to the tent, one gets lost on the land at night, or one walks up to a beast they don't know to fear and it turns on them.
